trips.title: Lake Towns of the Salzkammergut
trips.summary: Three lake towns in seven days, moved through by train and boat, with ceramics, salt mines and long afternoons on the water.

trips.title: West Flanders Squares, Bruges, Damme and Veurne
trips.summary: Four nights in Bruges and three in Veurne, moving by train and towpath, built around lace workshops and two of Flanders' best market squares.

trips.title: Herzegovina Slowly: Mostar, Blagaj, Počitelj & Trebinje
trips.summary: Herzegovina is stone, water and coffee, and the trick to it is refusing to do it in two days. This week gives you four nights in Mostar's old town and three in Trebinje, a plane-shaded southern town most visitors never reach, with the Ottoman villages of the Neretva, Blagaj, Počitelj, Stolac, filling the middle. The pace is set by the coffee ritual: a džezva, a fildžan, a sugar cube held in the teeth, and forty minutes that cannot be shortened. There is one town move, two afternoons with nothing in them, and a deliberate rule of arriving at the famous places either before 09:30 or after 17:00. It suits travellers who want the layered, complicated version of the Balkans rather than a bridge photograph.

trips.title: Carved Ceilings and Cobbled Bridges: A Slow Week in Bulgaria's Revival Towns
trips.sub: Sredna Gora, the Balkan foothills and the Veliko Tarnovo highlands
trips.summary: Three bases in seven days, and nothing that starts before nine. The *Vazrazhdane* towns are what Bulgaria built when it had money and no country: oriel windows overhanging cobbles, blue and ochre plaster, ceilings…

trips.title: Arcaded Squares of South Bohemia
trips.summary: Three arcaded Renaissance squares in seven days, Krumlov, Třeboň and Telč, with carp ponds, a Baroque theatre and two long lie-ins.

trips.title: South Funen Archipelago: Ærø, Faaborg & Svendborg
trips.summary: A seven-day cozy towns trip itinerary in Det Sydfynske Øhav (South Funen Archipelago), Denmark.

trips.title: Four Walled Villages of the Alsace Wine Road
trips.summary: Three fortified wine villages in seven days, nine kilometres apart, with grand cru footpaths, a 1715 cask and two mornings that start at ten.

trips.title: The Périgord Noir, Slowly
trips.summary: A slow week between Sarlat's market streets and the Vézère's river villages, with one relocation, walnut mills and honey-stone bastides.

trips.title: Franconian Squares, Rothenburg, Dinkelsbühl and the Ries
trips.summary: Three walled Franconian towns in seven days, Rothenburg, Dinkelsbühl and Nördlingen, with market mornings, Riemenschneider altars and only two moves.

trips.title: Slate and Riesling, The Mosel Village Week
trips.summary: Seven slow days between Bernkastel and Cochem, timber squares, slate vineyards, Fuder cellars and river boats, with only two moves all week.

trips.title: Pelion Kalderimia: Mansions, Plane Trees and the Little Train
trips.sub: Thessaly, Mount Pelion & the Pagasetic Gulf
trips.summary: Pelion is the mountain the centaurs were given, a 1,600 m ridge that drops on one side into the flat Pagasetic Gulf and on the other straight into the Aegean, and it is stitched together by *kalderimia*, cobbled mule paths, laid by hand, that were the only roads until the 1960s. The villages on it are unlike anywhere else in Greece: slate-roofed stone mansions with painted ceilings, built by a merchant class that got rich on silk and never quite left. This week uses three bases and no more, walks between villages rather than driving where possible, rides the metre-gauge Moutzouris train down to Milies, and spends deliberate hours doing nothing under thousand-year-old plane trees. It is a slow week by design: two moves, two long walks, several blocks of afternoon with nothing in them at all.

trips.title: The Bend and the Hills: Szentendre, Esztergom and the Palóc Villages
trips.sub: Danube Bend (Dunakanyar) & the Cserhát Hills, Nógrád County
trips.summary: Budapest is forty minutes behind you and it may as well be a different country. This week runs along the Danube where it turns hard south, Serbian church towers in Szentendre, a citadel above Visegrád, Hungary's…

trips.title: Umbrian Hill Towns: Spello, Bevagna & the Sagrantino Hills
trips.sub: Valle Umbra, Spello, Bevagna, Montefalco, Trevi
trips.summary: A week built around two squares and the hills between them. You settle into Spello for three nights and Bevagna for four; Montefalco's Sagrantino cellars, Trevi's olive presses and Rasiglia's water channels happen as half-day loops that return you to a familiar doorway before dark. The rhythm is deliberately Umbrian, shutters down 13:30-16:00, then the whole town reappearing on the corso at 18:30. Two town moves in seven days, two written-in "do nothing" blocks.

trips.title: Kurzeme Slow Week: Kuldīga, Sabile & Talsi
trips.summary: A seven-day cozy towns trip itinerary in Kurzeme (Courland), western Latvia, Latvia.

trips.title: Curonian Spit: Nida, Juodkrantė & the Dune Villages
trips.sub: Neringa / Klaipėda, Curonian Spit UNESCO World Heritage Site
trips.summary: A seven-day cozy towns trip itinerary in Neringa / Klaipėda, Curonian Spit UNESCO World Heritage Site, Lithuania.

trips.title: Little Switzerland and the Northern Castles
trips.summary: Echternach, Vianden and Clervaux in a week, on Luxembourg's free public transport, sandstone gorges, abbey squares and two hotel changes.

trips.title: The Round Fort and the Casa Mare: Seven Slow Days in Small-Town Moldova
trips.sub: The Middle Dniester, Soroca, and the Orhei Codru
trips.summary: Two towns, six nights split between them, and a lot of sitting down. Soroca has a perfectly circular fifteenth-century fort on the Dniester, six hundred steps up a cliff to a stone candle, and a hillside of…

trips.title: A Riviera Week from a Monaco Base
trips.summary: Monaco is 2 km² and takes a day and a half. Base there and let the Ventimiglia-Cannes railway deliver a different Riviera town every morning.

trips.title: The Hanseatic IJssel, Deventer, Zutphen, Zwolle, Hattem
trips.summary: Four Hanseatic towns on the IJssel in seven days, Friday and Saturday markets, chained libraries, bookshops and a single change of hotel.

trips.title: Ohrid, Bitola & Kruševo: Lake Light and Balkan Corso
trips.summary: North Macedonia rewards people who slow down further than they meant to. This week gives you four nights in Ohrid's stone old town above the lake, then three in Bitola, a former consular city with the best café street in the Balkans, with a single high day-trip up to Kruševo at 1,350 m. Everything else is squares, water and coffee that lasts an hour. The corso, the evening walk, is not a quaint survival here but the actual social infrastructure of both towns, and the itinerary is built around being in the right street when it happens. Two moves, two blank afternoons, and a country where a very good dinner costs €15.

trips.title: Loess, Arcades and Onion Bread: A Slow Week in Lubelskie's Small Towns
trips.sub: Lubelskie, the Vistula bend and the Zamość-Roztocze borderland
trips.summary: Eastern Poland's small towns keep different hours. A wooden well in the middle of a Renaissance square, ravines cut ten metres deep into pale loess by nothing but rainwater and cartwheels, a Gothic castle chapel…

trips.title: Alentejo's Walled Villages: Monsaraz, Estremoz & the Serra de São Mamede
trips.sub: Alentejo, Alqueva, Alto Alentejo & the marble towns
trips.summary: The Alentejo is Europe's great emptiness: cork oaks, wheat, marble quarries and villages walled against a threat that stopped mattering five hundred years ago. This week splits between two bases, four nights near Monsaraz above the Alqueva reservoir, three nights up at Castelo de Vide in the Serra de São Mamede, with a single move between them and long stretches where nothing is planned at all. You will buy pottery from the person who threw it, eat in a marble town on the day its market fills the square, and stand under one of the darkest skies in Europe. It suits travellers who find silence restful rather than boring, and who understand that an Alentejano lunch is a two-hour institution.

trips.title: Blue Gates and Fortified Churches: A Slow Week Through Saxon Transylvania
trips.sub: Târnava Mare & the Hârtibaciu Plateau, Saxon Transylvania (Siebenbürgen)
trips.summary: Seven days, four beds, and a lot of standing still. This is the Târnava Mare plateau: villages laid out by German settlers in the 12th century, each with one long street, one fortified church and a hill of hay meadow…

trips.title: San Marino & the Montefeltro: Towers, Truffles and Block-Printed Linen
trips.sub: San Marino & the Emilia-Romagna / Marche border
trips.summary: Two nights on a limestone crag that has been an independent republic since the fourth century, then four in the Malatesta hill country that surrounds it. San Marino is best understood as a strange, steep, self-governing village rather than a curiosity, and it is transformed the moment the last day-tripper takes the cable car down. Below it, the Montefeltro gives you San Leo's cliff fortress, Pennabilli's poet's gardens, Verucchio's Iron Age museum and Santarcangelo's tufa caves and printing workshop, all within a 40 km radius. One move, two open afternoons, and, if you time it for October, four Sundays of white truffle in Sant'Agata Feltria. It suits people who like small, dense places and don't need a coastline.

trips.title: Silver, Wood and Limewood: A Slow Week in Banská Štiavnica and the Spiš Towns
trips.summary: Slovakia keeps five UNESCO towns and villages within a comfortable day's drive of each other and almost nobody visits them in sequence. This is a week of three beds and long afternoons: a silver town inside a…

trips.title: Pueblos Blancos: Grazalema, Setenil & the Road Down to Vejer
trips.sub: Sierra de Grazalema & the Cádiz-Málaga white villages
trips.summary: Two bases, one long descent. You spend four nights high in Grazalema at 823 m, where the sierra rains hardest and the wool is still woven, then drop three nights to Vejer de la Frontera within sight of the Atlantic. In between are the villages that make the route famous, Zahara on its castle rock, Setenil built under an overhanging cliff, Olvera at the head of a disused railway now turned greenway. The pacing is unhurried by design: one move, two open afternoons, and no day that asks for more than 70 km of driving. It suits people who like a village square at 21:00, cheese bought from the person who made it, and a week where the best hours are the ones with nothing scheduled.

trips.title: Painted Houses, An Appenzellerland Week
trips.summary: Appenzell, Urnäsch, Stein and Gais in seven days, painted gables, working dairies, Biber bakers and narrow-gauge trains, with one hotel change.
